clue.text: Tory sleaze, without going to extremes, stirred up fanaticism

indicators.note: refusing to go to the extremes means the word loses its outermost letters at both ends
something stirred up is mixed around, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its first and last letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A political scandal about corrupt Conservatives whips up extreme passions.
explanation.walkthrough: Only sleaze loses its ends (S and E), leaving LEAZ to mix with TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealotry is the fervent, uncompromising attitude of a zealot, a close synonym for fanaticism.

clue.text: Unknown, with a burst of energy, becomes popular author

indicators.note: a burst scatters things, so the word after it lands in a different order

blocks.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
taken as written
taken as written, then mixed up

explanation.surface: A nobody, given a surge of vigour, turns into a bestselling writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zane Grey was an American novelist whose Western adventure stories sold in huge numbers.

clue.text: Decide undergarment held up's exotic attire

indicators.note: in a down clue, something held up reads from bottom to top
exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

blocks.note: a bra is an undergarment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion show where a raised bra counts as fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute by judgement, which is to decide between the parties.

clue.text: Charm award bestowed on a husband

blocks.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband is given an honour for his charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is Caribbean folk sorcery, and also a fetish or amulet used in it, so a magic charm.

clue.text: Holding up live ammunition — it's tied up again

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a round is a single cartridge of ammunition
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A gun battle with live rounds, and a captive tied up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live ammunition' is one phrase on the surface, but the two words are separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebound read as re-bound means bound a second time, that is fastened with ropes once more.

clue.text: Incentive to listen to Marlowe, say

indicators.note: asking us to listen means the sound of the name matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: Philip Marlowe is Raymond Chandler's private detective; 'say' marks him as an example bearing that first name

explanation.surface: A reason to tune in to a radio drama featuring the detective Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost that spurs someone on, which is what an incentive provides.

clue.text: Vamp is participating in rally

indicators.note: a word participating in another takes part within it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a patient or market that rallies improves
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seductive woman takes part in a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Vamp is not a seductress here but the musical verb: to play an improvised accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp in music is to make up a repeated accompaniment on the spot, which is to extemporise.

clue.text: You said plenty about bloomer

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the pronoun is represented by the letter that sounds like it
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: plenty means lots
the letter U is pronounced like the pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone told you there was lots to say about a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a mistake on the surface, but here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a plant that blooms, so playfully a bloomer.

clue.text: One boarding to go on illicit vessel

indicators.note: something boarding gets on and inside, so it is placed within the other word

blocks.note: to prate is to go on, talking at tedious length
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A smuggler boarding an outlaw ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One boarding' looks like the definition, a raider; but the defined thing is the ship itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate can be the ship as well as the sailor, a vessel operating outside the law.

clue.text: Old master uses book on English in courses

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the following word

blocks.note: a run is a course, as in a ski run
B is the abbreviation for book
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A veteran teacher uses an English textbook in his classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts book before English, as in down clues one piece sits on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a 17th-century Flemish painter, one of the great old masters.

clue.text: Old coin, by no means common

blocks.note: first meaning: a gold coin minted in England from the 14th to 16th centuries
second meaning: of aristocratic rank rather than a commoner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like it describes the coin's rarity, but it means belonging to the ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes aristocratic birth, the opposite of commoners, and the noun names a medieval English gold piece.

clue.text: Flag down fisherman

blocks.note: feeling down is feeling blue
the apostle Peter was a fisherman

explanation.surface: A tired fisherman flags, or someone lowers a flag on a fishing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag down' reads as hailing a vehicle; split it so 'Flag' is the definition and 'down' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is the blue-and-white signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Go and see hut, a dilapidated building

indicators.note: a dilapidated structure has fallen to pieces, so these letters are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit a tumbledown shed on someone's land.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is a small building at an entrance gate, often a lodge on an estate.

clue.text: Assault is beginning

blocks.note: first meaning: an attack
second meaning: the start of something, such as an illness

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as news that an attack is starting; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military onslaught and the first appearance or start of something.

clue.text: Awfully pleased to have passed

indicators.note: something done awfully is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to have got through an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' suggests success in a test, but it means time has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time has elapsed it has slipped away or gone by, the temporal sense of passed.

clue.text: Singer performing, with the cast milling around

indicators.note: a crowd milling around moves about aimlessly, so these letters change places

blocks.note: a performer on stage is on
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist on stage while the rest of the company wanders about.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is a songbird, not a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird, and birds that sing are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Second chance to cut

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to chance on something is to light on it

explanation.surface: A second opportunity to trim something, or a retake in a film edit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them pointedly, and a slight is exactly that kind of snub.

clue.text: The vulgar rhyme

blocks.note: surface reading: a coarse or bawdy piece of verse
setter's reading: the common people, named by a Greek phrase whose two words chime with each other

explanation.walkthrough: 'The vulgar' is a noun, the common herd, and 'rhyme' points out that the Greek phrase rhymes internally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek expression means 'the many' and is used in English for the masses, the common folk.

clue.text: Laugh about girl beginning to cause worrying problem

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh wraps round what follows
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: he-he is a laugh
Ada is a girl's name
first letter only

explanation.surface: Mocking a girl starts to create real trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is figuratively a nagging difficulty, the kind of problem that keeps someone anxious.

clue.text: Promote business in dispatch

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits within it, so the company goes inside the dispatching word

blocks.note: to dispatch is to send
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: Advance a company's interests through prompt delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it formally, supporting and furthering it as promote implies.

clue.text: Commit matricide in field?

blocks.note: to do someone in is slang for murder, the deed committed
the victim of matricide is one's mother, Ma

explanation.surface: Asking whether a murder of a mother happened in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'commit matricide' as the instruction 'do Ma in', and the words run together; there is no separate indicator, the phrase itself places Ma inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a sphere of activity or knowledge, which is what a field of expertise is.

clue.text: Exercise control before assuming pretentious air?

blocks.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
side is dated slang for a pretentious, superior manner, as in 'putting on side'

explanation.surface: A boss takes charge only after adopting a haughty manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Side meaning swank or affected airs is old British slang; 'assuming' just means putting it on.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair a meeting or be in charge, which means holding authority over proceedings.

clue.text: Dish's burning as result of being careless with fire

definitions.text: result of being careless with fire

blocks.note: a pot is a dish, and 's adds the S
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: A dish is scorched because someone was careless with the flame.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire here is gunfire, not a cooking flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot shot is a casual, unaimed shot, the outcome of shooting carelessly rather than taking aim.

clue.text: Ark put up for sale after a century

indicators.note: after says the sale phrase follows the hundred, setting the order of the two pieces

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to offer something is to put it up for sale

explanation.surface: An antique chest goes on sale after a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: An ark in the older sense is a chest or box, and a coffer is a strongbox for valuables.

clue.text: Part of brooch, red and yellow

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters inside these two words

explanation.surface: Describing a piece of jewellery set with red and yellow stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like part of a colour definition, but it supplies the last letters of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment, typically a dull yellow-brown, used since prehistory for painting.

clue.text: Lots of women hasten to get married

blocks.note: to hare is to run fast
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Many women are in a hurry to find husbands.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives and concubines in a polygamous household, a large collection of women.

clue.text: Fellow, brought up to bowl, shivers

blocks.note: a fellow is a counterpart or equal, as is a match
in the game of bowls the balls are called woods

explanation.surface: A cricketer called on to bowl is trembling with nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shivers' is not trembling but a noun: splinters, as in 'shiver my timbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood means wood smashed into tiny splinters, and shivers are fragments or slivers of a broken object.

clue.text: Greeting man will love

blocks.note: he'll is short for he will
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A man who receives a greeting will fall in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard word said on meeting someone, a common salutation.

clue.text: Out of the medals, we hear, despite showing right away

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the place in the race is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: finishing fourth misses gold, silver and bronze
with can mean in spite of, as in 'with all his faults'

explanation.surface: An athlete off the podium nevertheless performs well straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith is a formal word meaning immediately, without any delay at all.

clue.text: In the course of visit, one turned purple

indicators.note: something in the course of another happens during it, so one piece sits inside the other
turned round, the whole combination is read from the other end

blocks.note: to call on someone is to visit
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: During a social call, someone went red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is the pale mauve colour of the shrub's flowers, a light shade of purple.

clue.text: Engineers spot on? It's unlikely

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a mote is a tiny speck; 'on' places it after the engineers

explanation.surface: Doubt over whether a team of engineers is exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot on' reads as 'exactly correct', but spot is a speck and 'on' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is a slim one, so describing an outcome as remote says it is improbable.

clue.text: Drug abuse — a pointer

indicators.note: abuse is mistreatment, and these letters are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tip-off about drug abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a poisonous alkaloid from deadly nightshade, used medically to dilate pupils.
